name: Andhra Pradesh: Araku valley, Lambasingi and Gandikota
one_line: Andhra Pradesh, the Eastern Ghats above Visakhapatnam and the Penna river gorge at Gandikota

source.title: Gandikota Canyon Andhra Pradesh: India's Hidden Grand Canyon Travel Guide 2026

fuel.note: Pumps are those drawn on the open map within the search radius of the road. A pump missing from the map is missing here, so each gap is a worst case.

rules.title: Ghat roads: heavy vehicles barred at night in fog
rules.detail: In December 2025 police barred heavy goods and passenger vehicles from the district's ghat roads from 10 pm to 5 am. Other drivers were told to slow down.
rules.applies_to: Heavy vehicles; advice only for light vehicles and two-wheelers
rules.set_by: Superintendent of Police, Alluri Sitharama Raju district

source.title: Cops Ban Night travel for Heavy Vehicles on ASR Ghat Road

history.change: Night ban imposed after a bus fell off the Chintur to Maredumilli ghat road, to last until fog eased. No end date was reported.

source.title: Night ban on heavy vehicles on ASR ghat roads after bus tragedy

rules.title: Gandikota fort: daytime entry, no entry fee
rules.detail: A travel blog gives fort hours as 9 am to 6 pm with free entry; camping and activities are charged by operators. No government page was found.

source.title: Gandikota Canyon Andhra Pradesh: India's Hidden Grand Canyon Travel Guide 2026

season.note: October to February is the usual window; the hills get most of their rain from June to October and Gandikota is very hot from March to June.

authorities.office: Superintendent of Police, Alluri Sitharama Raju district
authorities.announces: Traffic orders for the ghat roads, such as night bans in fog
authorities.stretch: Araku, Paderu and Lambasingi ghat roads
authorities.channel: Police order, reported in the press

source.title: Cops Ban Night travel for Heavy Vehicles on ASR Ghat Road

hazards.title: Dense winter fog on the ghat roads
hazards.detail: Fog in the hill district led police to bar heavy vehicles at night in December 2025 and to tell all drivers to slow down.

source.title: Cops Ban Night travel for Heavy Vehicles on ASR Ghat Road

hazards.title: Near-freezing winter nights at Lambasingi
hazards.detail: At about 1,000 metres, winter temperatures on rare occasions fall below freezing; mornings are foggy.

hazards.title: Heavy rain in the Araku hills
hazards.detail: Araku gets about 1,700 millimetres of rain a year, most of it between June and October.

hazards.title: Roadworks on the hill highway
hazards.detail: The highway from Koyyuru through Lambasingi, Paderu and Araku is being widened under a national project.

hazards.title: Summer heat and open cliff edges at Gandikota
hazards.detail: March to June days are very hot, and the gorge viewpoints have unprotected edges; visit in daylight.

source.title: Gandikota Canyon Andhra Pradesh: India's Hidden Grand Canyon Travel Guide 2026

gaps: No official page was found for any rule at Araku, Paderu, Lambasingi or Gandikota. The one dated order recorded is a police order reported in the press.
Whether the December 2025 night ban on heavy vehicles is still in force, and which ghat roads it names, was not stated in the reports read.

Highest point: Lambasingi is the only place on the road with a sourced height. Wikipedia gives two different heights for Araku Valley. Arma Konda, 1,680 metres, is the state's highest peak and lies north of Paderu, off the road.
No source found for the road from Visakhapatnam up to Araku or for the long link between the hills and Gandikota.
No source found for fuel gaps in the hill stretch or for landslides on the Araku ghat road.
Usual number of riding days: no source found.
Videos: the pages give upload dates, not filming dates, so 'filmed' is filled only where the title names a date. Uploads, in order: 2026-03, 2022-11.
